dialog.body: Finance, this is Luis. How can I help you?
Hello, yes. My name is Maureen Sullivan. I got a parking ticket on Saturday, and I think it was written in error. I would like to know how to contest it.
Okay, sure, I can walk you through that. Do you have the ticket in front of you?
I do. One moment. [pause] Sorry, I am doing this on the computer also, and my mouse stopped working yesterday, so I am using the trackpad. It is going very badly. I keep clicking the wrong thing.
Trackpads are a punishment. Take your time. What's the ticket number at the top?
The number is in the upper right corner. It starts with two letters, P and K, and then seven digits. Four, four, one, zero, eight, two, nine.
PK4410829. Got it. Let me pull that up. And what's the violation it says?

It says, um, parking in a resident permit only space without a permit displayed. But that is the problem. I have the sticker. It is on the windshield, the lower corner on the passenger side, where it is supposed to be. I checked this morning, it is still there, it did not fall off.
Okay. And was the sticker current, for this year?

Yes, of course current. I got it in January, I have the receipt also. The car is registered here, I am a homeowner. So I do not understand how the officer did not see it. It is not hidden. It is not small.
Yeah, that's a fair thing to be annoyed about. Was it raining Saturday when you parked?

Yes, it was raining, that rain from Friday into Saturday. But the windshield is still a windshield. You can see through it, the officer could see the sticker if he looked. I think maybe he just looked at the plate and not the glass.
Could be. Either way, the way you handle this is an appeal. You'd send in the ticket number, a statement of what happened, and a photo of the sticker on the windshield if you can get one.
A photo, okay. I can take that today. With the phone, not with the computer, because the computer is being difficult. Should the photo show the whole car?

Best if it shows the sticker in place on the glass and, if you can, the plate or the car in the same shot. Then a second close-up so they can read the sticker. And a copy of the registration or that receipt you mentioned.
Okay. Registration, receipt, two photos. I am writing it down. And how long does the appeal take? Because the ticket has a date, and I do not want it to double while I wait.

So generally it takes a few weeks to get a decision, depends how backed up they are. What matters is that you file before the due date on the ticket. Once an appeal is in, the ticket is on hold while it's reviewed.
A few weeks. Okay. And the due date is, let me find it, [pause] the trackpad again. Sorry. It says the twenty-fourth of this month.
The twenty-fourth. You've got two weeks, plenty of time if you get it in this week or next. I'd do it this week.
Yes, this week. Do I send it by mail, or is there a form I fill out?
There's a back side to the ticket with the appeal instructions, and you can also come in and drop it with us here at the window. Check the back, it should list the mailing address.
Let me turn it over. [pause] Yes, there is a paragraph. It is very small print. I will read it with the glasses. It says a written request. Okay. So I write a letter, basically.
Basically, yep. Keep it short and factual. Your name, the ticket number, the plate, what happened, and what you're attaching.
Good. I can be factual. I am very factual. I just do not like paying for somebody else's mistake, even a small one.
Understood. If the photos are clear, you've got a solid case, a sticker on the windshield is about as clean as it gets.
One more thing. Do I need to pay anything now to file the appeal? Or is it only after, if they say no?
You don't need to pay to file the appeal as far as I know. If they uphold it, the decision letter will tell you what's owed and by when.
Okay. And they will send the answer by mail?
Mail, yes, to the address you put on the letter. So make sure that's right, and put your phone number on there too in case they have a question.
I will put the phone number. It is the same one I am calling from. Do you need it for your notes?
Sure, go ahead, I'll note it on the ticket record.
It is four-oh-one, five-five-five, zero-one-seven-two.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-seven-two. Got it, it's noted. That way if your letter and my note ever meet, they'll agree with each other.
That would be a nice change. Thank you. So, photos today, letter tomorrow, drop it at the window.
That's the plan. Window's open during regular business hours, and just ask for the ticket appeals pile.
Okay. Thank you for the explanation, Mr. Barros. Now I go fight with my trackpad.
Good luck with that one. You take care, Ms. Sullivan.
Goodbye.
